title: Generic Functions
concept: Generic functions use type parameters to work with multiple types — write once, use with any type that satisfies the constraints.
why: The most common form of generics. Every time you find yourself copying a function to change the type, a generic function is the answer.
syntax_ref:
fn name[T](param: T) -> T { /* body */ }
fn name[T: Constraint](param: T) -> ReturnType { /* body */ }
tips: Let type inference work — you rarely need to write first[Int] explicitly
Generic functions should be truly generic — avoid assuming anything about T without a constraint
Test generic functions with at least 2-3 different types to ensure they're truly type-agnostic
common_mistakes: Using type-specific operations (like + or ==) without adding the corresponding constraint
Forgetting that [] creates an empty Vec, not a type parameter — use fn f[T] for generics
Putting type parameters on non-generic functions — only add [T] if you actually use T
